subtopics.name: Power, Authority, Legitimacy, and Sovereignty
objectives: Define power, authority, legitimacy, and sovereignty.
Distinguish between traditional, charismatic, and legal-rational authority.
Explain how legitimacy sustains political sovereignty.

subtopics.name: State, Society, Nation, and Political Processes
objectives: Distinguish between society, state, nation, and nation-state.
Explain political socialization, participation, and political culture.
Analyze how political culture shapes governance and citizen behavior.

subtopics.name: Democratic and Non-Democratic Systems
objectives: Distinguish between democracy, monarchy, oligarchy, aristocracy, and theocracy.
Compare direct and representative democracy.
Evaluate the merits and demerits of each form of government.

subtopics.name: Totalitarianism, Fascism, and Military Government
objectives: Explain the features of totalitarian and fascist governments.
Assess the characteristics and impact of military rule.
Compare authoritarian and democratic governance models.

subtopics.name: Legislature and Executive
objectives: Explain the structure, powers, and functions of the legislature.
Describe the roles and powers of the executive arm.
Analyze the relationship between the legislature and executive.

subtopics.name: The Judiciary and Separation of Powers
objectives: Describe the structure and functions of the judiciary.
Explain the doctrine of separation of powers and checks and balances.
Evaluate the independence of the judiciary in democratic governance.

subtopics.name: Unitary and Federal Systems
objectives: Distinguish between unitary and federal systems of government.
Identify the features and merits of each structure.
Evaluate examples of unitary and federal states.

subtopics.name: Confederal System and Devolution of Power
objectives: Explain the features of a confederal system.
Discuss devolution of power and its effects.
Compare devolved, federal, and unitary governance.

subtopics.name: Presidential and Parliamentary Systems
objectives: Distinguish between the presidential and parliamentary systems.
Identify the key features, merits, and demerits of each.
Describe examples of countries using each system.

subtopics.name: Constitutional Monarchy and Hybrid Systems
objectives: Explain the concept of constitutional monarchy.
Distinguish between hybrid governance systems.
Assess the effectiveness of different systems of governance.

subtopics.name: Capitalism, Socialism, and Communism
objectives: Define and distinguish capitalism, socialism, and communism.
Compare modes of production under each ideology.
Assess the practical impact of these ideologies on governance.

subtopics.name: Liberalism, Conservatism, and Fascism
objectives: Explain the core tenets of liberalism, conservatism, and fascism.
Contrast liberal and conservative approaches to governance.
Evaluate how political ideologies shape economic and social policy.

subtopics.name: Definition, Sources, and Functions of Constitutions
objectives: Define a constitution and identify its sources.
Explain the functions of a constitution in a democratic state.
Distinguish between written and unwritten constitutions.

subtopics.name: Rigid and Flexible Constitutions
objectives: Compare rigid and flexible constitutions with examples.
Explain the process of constitutional amendment.
Evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of each constitutional type.

subtopics.name: Rule of Law, Fundamental Rights, and Constitutionalism
objectives: Identify and explain the principles of democratic government.
Describe the rule of law and its application in governance.
Explain the protection of fundamental human rights.

subtopics.name: Free and Fair Elections, and Accountability
objectives: Explain the importance of free and fair elections in democracy.
Describe mechanisms of accountability and transparency.
Assess how democratic principles are applied in practice.

subtopics.name: Stages of a Bill
objectives: Outline the stages involved in passing a bill into law.
Distinguish between public and private bills.
Explain the roles of the two legislative chambers in enacting laws.

subtopics.name: Types of Laws and Legislative Powers
objectives: Identify different types of laws (statutory, delegated, customary).
Explain the concept of delegated legislation.
Assess the limits and scope of legislative authority.

subtopics.name: Acquisition and Loss of Citizenship
objectives: Differentiate between methods of acquiring citizenship (birth, naturalization, registration).
Explain conditions under which citizenship may be revoked.
Distinguish between citizens, aliens, and stateless persons.

subtopics.name: Rights, Duties, and Obligations
objectives: Specify the rights and responsibilities of a citizen.
Assess the obligations of the state to its citizens.
Evaluate civic duties and their importance to national development.

subtopics.name: Franchise and Electoral Systems
objectives: Distinguish between universal adult suffrage and restricted franchise.
Identify and explain types of electoral systems (proportional, first-past-the-post).
Compare the merits and demerits of different electoral systems.

subtopics.name: Electoral Commissions and Electoral Processes
objectives: Describe the role of the electoral commission in managing elections.
Outline the stages of the electoral process from voting to declaration.
Analyze factors that affect the credibility and integrity of elections.

subtopics.name: Functions and Organization of Political Parties
objectives: Assess the role and importance of political parties in democracy.
Describe the typical structure and organization of a political party.
Explain how parties recruit members and formulate policies.

subtopics.name: Party Systems: One-Party, Two-Party, Multi-Party
objectives: Distinguish between one-party, two-party, and multi-party systems.
Compare the advantages and disadvantages of each party system.
Give examples of countries associated with each party system.

subtopics.name: Functions and Modus Operandi of Pressure Groups
objectives: Evaluate the functions and methods of pressure groups.
Distinguish between protective and promotional pressure groups.
Analyze examples of pressure groups in Nigeria and elsewhere.

subtopics.name: Pressure Groups vs Political Parties
objectives: Distinguish between pressure groups and political parties.
Assess the influence of pressure groups on government policy.
Discuss the limitations and criticism of pressure group activities.

subtopics.name: Formation and Measurement of Public Opinion
objectives: Compare methods of assessing public opinion (polls, surveys, media).
Analyze how public opinion is formed and shaped.
Assess the functions of public opinion in democratic governance.

subtopics.name: Limitations and Role of the Media
objectives: Analyze the limitations of public opinion as a political force.
Explain the role of the mass media in shaping public opinion.
Evaluate propaganda and its effect on public political attitudes.

subtopics.name: Structure, Functions, and Principles of the Civil Service
objectives: Analyze the significance and functions of the civil service in governance.
Describe the hierarchical structure of the civil service.
Explain the principles of neutrality, permanence, and anonymity.

subtopics.name: Civil Service Reforms and Challenges
objectives: Identify major reforms in the Nigerian civil service.
Assess the challenges facing the civil service.
Evaluate the impact of bureaucracy on government efficiency.

subtopics.name: Hausa, Yoruba, and Igbo Pre-colonial Systems
objectives: Appreciate the effectiveness of the pre-colonial political systems.
Describe the governance structures of Hausa Emirates, Yoruba kingdoms, and Igbo communities.
Compare centralized and segmentary pre-colonial systems.

subtopics.name: Other Nigerian Pre-colonial States
objectives: Describe pre-colonial governance in Benin, Kanuri, Nupe, and Tiv societies.
Compare monarchical and republican elements in pre-colonial governance.
Assess the legacy of pre-colonial political institutions on modern Nigeria.

subtopics.name: British and French Colonial Policies
objectives: Trace the processes of imperialist penetration in West Africa.
Assess the impact of British indirect rule and French assimilation policies.
Distinguish between British and French colonial administrative practices.

subtopics.name: Amalgamation and Colonial Administration in Nigeria
objectives: Explain the amalgamation of Northern and Southern Nigeria in 1914.
Describe the structure of British colonial government in Nigeria.
Assess the social and political impact of colonialism on Nigerian society.

subtopics.name: Nationalism and Independence Movements
objectives: Evaluate the process of decolonization in Nigeria and Africa.
Assess the roles of nationalist leaders and political parties.
Analyze the significance of Pan-Africanism and the Back-to-Africa movement.

subtopics.name: External Forces and the Push for Independence
objectives: Assess the impact of the Second World War on African independence movements.
Explain the role of the United Nations in the decolonization process.
Evaluate how international pressure contributed to Nigeria's independence.

subtopics.name: Clifford, Richards, and Macpherson Constitutions
objectives: Compare the Clifford (1922), Richards (1946), and Macpherson (1951) constitutions.
Identify the major features and limitations of each constitution.
Analyze how each constitution moved Nigeria toward self-governance.

subtopics.name: Lyttleton Constitution and Independence Constitution
objectives: Describe the Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 and its federal provisions.
Explain the Independence Constitution of 1960.
Assess the role of constitutional development in Nigeria's independence.

subtopics.name: Republican Constitution of 1963 and Decree 34 of 1966
objectives: Assess the workings of the 1963 Republican Constitution.
Describe the impact of the Unification Decree of 1966.
Identify major political crises that triggered constitutional changes.

subtopics.name: 1979, 1989, and 1999 Constitutions
objectives: Compare the 1979 and 1999 constitutions as presidential systems.
Explain the provisions of the 1989 and 1995 draft constitutions.
Evaluate recurring constitutional issues in post-independence Nigeria.

topics.name: Institutions of Government in Post-Independence Nigeria

subtopics.name: Legislature, Executive, and Judiciary in Post-Independence Nigeria
objectives: Evaluate the operations of the National Assembly and State Assemblies.
Describe the powers and functions of the Presidency and State Governors.
Assess the role of the judiciary in post-independence governance.

subtopics.name: Security Agencies and Administrative Bodies
objectives: Explain the roles of the Armed Forces, Police, and NSCDC.
Describe the functions of key administrative agencies.
Assess the effectiveness of institutional governance in Nigeria.

subtopics.name: Functions and Operations of Public Commissions
objectives: Evaluate the operations of major public commissions (INEC, RMAFC, NPC, etc.).
Identify the roles and powers of each commission.
Assess the importance of independent commissions in democratic governance.

subtopics.name: Challenges and Constraints of Public Commissions
objectives: Assess the problems facing public commissions in Nigeria.
Identify constraints such as executive interference and funding.
Propose ways to strengthen the independence of public commissions.

subtopics.name: First and Second Republic Political Parties
objectives: Contrast political processes in the First and Second Republics.
Evaluate the ideologies, structure, and composition of major parties (NCNC, AG, NPC, NPN, UPN, NPP).
Assess the role of ethnicity and regionalism in Nigerian party politics.

subtopics.name: Third and Fourth Republic Political Parties
objectives: Describe the party transition programs of Babangida and Abacha.
Identify dominant political parties of the Fourth Republic (PDP, APC, etc.).
Evaluate the evolution of multiparty democracy in modern Nigeria.

topics.name: Structure and Workings of Nigerian Federalism

subtopics.name: Features and Principles of Nigerian Federalism
objectives: Examine the key features and workings of Nigerian federalism.
Identify powers assigned to federal, state, and concurrent legislative lists.
Describe the revenue allocation formula and its evolution.

subtopics.name: Problems and Corrective Measures in Nigerian Federalism
objectives: Identify the major problems facing Nigerian federalism (resource control, imbalance).
Evaluate corrective measures adopted (state creation, constitutional conferences).
Assess the relationship between the federal and state governments.

subtopics.name: Operations and Purpose of Public Corporations
objectives: Examine the operations and economic rationale of public corporations.
Identify major Nigerian parastatals (NNPC, NERC, CBN, etc.).
Assess the role of public corporations in national development.

subtopics.name: Privatization and Commercialization
objectives: Identify the processes involved in privatization and commercialization.
Assess the economic importance and impact of privatization in Nigeria.
Evaluate arguments for and against the privatization of public enterprises.

subtopics.name: Evolution, Structure, and Functions of Local Government
objectives: Trace the evolution of local government in Nigeria from colonial times.
Describe the structure and functions of local government councils.
Explain the 1976 Local Government Reform and its significance.

subtopics.name: Problems and Reforms of Local Government
objectives: Identify the major problems faced by local governments (inadequate funding, state interference).
Evaluate the impact of local government reforms on grassroots governance.
Assess the relationship between local, state, and federal governments.

subtopics.name: Reasons for Military Intervention
objectives: Evaluate the reasons given for military intervention in Nigerian politics.
Identify constitutional provisions for civilian control of the military.
Assess the impact of coups on democratic governance in Nigeria.

subtopics.name: Achievements and Withdrawal of Military Rule
objectives: Assess the achievements and failures of military administrations.
Determine the conditions that necessitated military withdrawal from governance.
Evaluate the role of international pressure, civil society, and NADECO in the transition.

subtopics.name: Definition and Determinants of Foreign Policy
objectives: Define foreign policy and distinguish it from domestic policy.
Identify and explain the determinants of foreign policy (geography, economy, ideology).
Evaluate the instruments used to implement foreign policy.

subtopics.name: Types and Goals of Foreign Policy
objectives: Distinguish between bilateral and multilateral foreign policy.
Explain the goals of foreign policy: security, economic cooperation, and diplomacy.
Assess the role of international law and diplomacy in foreign policy.

subtopics.name: Objectives and Principles of Nigeria's Foreign Policy
objectives: Identify the major objectives of Nigeria's foreign policy.
Explain Nigeria's non-aligned posture during the Cold War.
Assess the principle of Africa as the centerpiece of Nigeria's foreign policy.

subtopics.name: Nigeria's Foreign Policy in Practice
objectives: Evaluate Nigeria's role in conflict resolution and peacekeeping.
Assess Nigeria's economic diplomacy and international trade relations.
Analyze changes in Nigeria's foreign policy from independence to present.

subtopics.name: Nigeria's Role in Continental African Affairs
objectives: Evaluate the role of Nigeria in continental affairs.
Describe Nigeria's contributions to OAU/AU, ECOWAS, and ECOMOG.
Assess the impact of Nigeria's foreign aid and technical cooperation in Africa.

subtopics.name: NEPAD and Regional Development
objectives: Assess the role of NEPAD in developing Africa.
Explain Nigeria's contributions to regional integration and development.
Evaluate challenges to African unity and Nigeria's diplomatic responses.

subtopics.name: United Nations and its Specialized Agencies
objectives: Evaluate the structure, operations, and functions of the United Nations.
Identify the roles of key UN agencies (UNESCO, WHO, UNICEF, etc.).
Assess the UN's role in maintaining international peace and security.

subtopics.name: AU, ECOWAS, Commonwealth, and Other Bodies
objectives: Evaluate the operations of regional and international organizations (AU, ECOWAS, Commonwealth, Non-Aligned Movement).
Assess the role of these organizations in world affairs.
Appreciate the challenges of international organizations and how they can be overcome.
